name: abap2ui5
description: Develop abap2UI5 apps in VS Code: F9 launches a z2ui5_if_app class in an embedded preview, reload on activation, static view checks, the abap2UI5 MCP server for AI agents, snippets.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The view check, the MCP server, the report converter and the browser logon can be told which program to start, one setting allows AI agents to operate apps on the system as you and one decides whether each of their steps is put to you first, one lets the auth proxy accept every unverified TLS certificate and one decides which build of the render gate is downloaded. Those settings are read from your user settings only, so a repository cannot point them at something else. The launch settings, which decide the host F9 and the credential prompt talk to, and the switch that turns the render gate on are ignored from the workspace in Restricted Mode; a trusted workspace can set them, so a team can share its systems in the repository - and the render gate does not run in Restricted Mode at all. The MCP server, the unit-test runner and the report converter do start processes (the runner does not start at all in Restricted Mode: the tests are the repository's code), which is why this is limited rather than unconditional.

languageModelTools.name: abap2ui5_get_view_findings
languageModelTools.userDescription: The abap2UI5 view check's findings for the active file, as the Problems panel shows them.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the abap2UI5 view check's findings for one document - an abap2UI5 app class (*.clas.abap) or an XML view - exactly as the editor's Problems panel shows them: rule id, severity, 1-based line and message per finding. Defaults to the active editor; pass `uri` for another document. It reads what the editor has already published and does not run a check: a file that is neither open nor covered by the last "Check All Views in the Workspace" has no findings to report. Read-only.

uri.description: The document's URI (file:///..., or the URI of a class opened from a system), or an absolute file path. Omit it for the active editor.

languageModelTools.name: abap2ui5_get_reconstructed_view
languageModelTools.userDescription: The XML view an abap2UI5 app class builds, reconstructed from its builder chain.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the XML view(s) an abap2UI5 app class builds with z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder, reconstructed statically from the class source - the same document "Show Reconstructed XML View" opens. Use it to see the control tree, properties and bindings a builder chain produces without running the app. Defaults to the active editor; pass `uri` for another class. Read-only; no system is contacted.

uri.description: The document's URI (file:///..., or the URI of a class opened from a system), or an absolute file path. Omit it for the active editor.

languageModelTools.name: abap2ui5_get_running_app_model
languageModelTools.userDescription: The live JSON model of the app shown in the abap2UI5 preview.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the live JSON model of the abap2UI5 app currently shown in the editor's embedded preview - the values the running app actually holds, as the preview's { } button shows them. Use it to answer why a bound control is empty or shows an unexpected value. Takes no input. Answers with a plain sentence when no app is running in the preview. A large model is cut at 50 KB and the answer says so. Read-only: it asks the page already loaded and sends nothing to the system.

abap2ui5.launchUrlTemplate.markdownDescription:
URL template used to launch an abap2UI5 app. The `{class}` placeholder is replaced with the (upper-cased) class name.

Example: `https://host:44300/sap/bc/z2ui5?app_start={class}&sap-client=100`

For more than one system use `#abap2ui5.systems#` instead - this setting is the single-system shorthand and stays the first entry of the list.

name.description: Shown in the picker and the status bar, e.g. DEV or Sandbox.

url.description: Launch URL template with the {class} placeholder.

role.description: What the system is used for. On a production system the agent app tools refuse app_start and app_act, and the status bar shows the role. Optional.

minUi5.description: The UI5 version this system serves, e.g. 1.120. While the system is active it replaces abap2ui5.viewCheck.minUi5; a repository's abap2ui5lint.jsonc still wins. Optional.

distribution.description: The UI5 distribution this system serves. While the system is active it replaces abap2ui5.viewCheck.distribution; a repository's abap2ui5lint.jsonc still wins. Optional.

enumDescriptions: User and password, asked for once per host and kept in the VS Code SecretStorage (the default).

An X.509 client certificate (.pfx/.p12, or PEM certificate and key) you choose per host with "abap2UI5: Choose Client Certificate"; the system maps it to your user. Only the file path (machine-local) and the passphrase (SecretStorage) are stored.

A logon in a browser window the extension opens (the render gate's Chromium, or abap2ui5.logon.browserExecutable): whatever the system asks for - SAML 2.0 single sign-on, Kerberos, a certificate from the OS store, the logon form - happens there, and the session cookies are kept in memory for this VS Code window only. Nothing is stored.
auth.description: How the auth proxy logs on to this system. A host you set to "certificate" or "browser" in your user settings keeps it when a workspace lists the same host without it.

abap2ui5.systems.markdownDescription:
The systems F9 can launch against. The active one is picked with the command **"abap2UI5: Select System"** and is remembered per window, so two windows can work against two systems at once. Credentials are stored per host, so switching does not ask again. An entry may also name the UI5 version and distribution its system serves (`minUi5`, `distribution` - used by the view check while that system is active) and its `role` (`"production"`: the agent app tools refuse to act there).

```json
[
  { "name": "DEV", "url": "https://dev:44300/sap/bc/z2ui5?app_start={class}&sap-client=100", "minUi5": "1.120", "distribution": "sapui5" },
  { "name": "Sandbox", "url": "https://box:44300/sap/bc/z2ui5?app_start={class}" },
  { "name": "PRD", "url": "https://prd:44300/sap/bc/z2ui5?app_start={class}", "role": "production" }
]
```

Optional per system: `minUi5` and `distribution` - what that system serves; while it is the active system they replace `#abap2ui5.viewCheck.minUi5#` and `#abap2ui5.viewCheck.distribution#` (a repository's `abap2ui5lint.jsonc` wins over both). `role`: `"development"` or `"production"` - on a production system the agent app tools refuse to start or operate apps, and the status bar shows the role; a system you marked as production in your user settings stays production when a workspace lists the same host without the mark. `auth`: `"basic"` (user and password, the default) or `"certificate"` (an X.509 client certificate you choose per host with **"abap2UI5: Choose Client Certificate"**) - a mechanism other than basic that your user settings name for a host stays in effect when a workspace lists the same host without it. A field with a value the extension does not understand is ignored and named in the *abap2UI5* output.

abap2ui5.allowUnauthorizedCerts.markdownDescription:
Accept **every** TLS certificate that cannot be verified - self-signed certificates, private CAs not in the OS trust store, hostname mismatches - on **every** system, without asking. Off by default.

You normally do not need this: when a system's certificate cannot be verified, F9 and **"abap2UI5: Check System Connection"** show the certificate (subject, issuer, validity, SHA-256 fingerprint) and ask once whether to trust it. A trusted certificate is accepted for that system only, and the connection is refused if the system ever presents a different one. **"abap2UI5: Forget Trusted Certificates"** drops those answers. A system with a certificate from a public CA is never asked about.

**Security tradeoff:** while this is enabled, the connection to the system is encrypted but not authenticated - a machine-in-the-middle could present its own certificate and read the traffic, including the SAP credentials the local auth proxy injects.

This setting is read from your user settings only - a cloned repository cannot switch certificate verification off for you.

abap2ui5.logon.browserExecutable.markdownDescription:
The browser a system with `"auth": "browser"` logs on in - the full path of a Chrome, Edge or Chromium executable. Empty (the default): the Chromium **"abap2UI5: Install Render Gate"** downloads. The browser is started with a fresh, temporary profile that is deleted after the logon, controlled over a pipe (no network port); the session cookies it hands over are kept in memory for this VS Code window only.

This setting is read from your user settings only - a cloned repository cannot choose which program is started.

abap2ui5.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show *Run*, *Activate & reload*, *Check views* and *Autofix n findings* above the class definition of an abap2UI5 app. The autofix lens appears only while the view check has findings it can correct mechanically.

enumDescriptions: Embedded in an editor tab, through the local auth proxy (with login).
Embedded in the bottom panel, through the local auth proxy (with login).
Open in the default browser (reuses your existing SAP session/SSO).
abap2ui5.openMode.markdownDescription:
How F9 opens the app.

- `tab`: embedded in an editor tab. Runs through a **local auth proxy** that injects your SAP credentials (asked for once) - no 401.
- `panel`: the same, but in the bottom panel area - the **abap2UI5 Preview** tab next to Terminal and Output.
- `external`: in the normal browser (reuses your existing login, no proxy needed).

The commands **"abap2UI5: Show the Preview in the Panel"** and **"abap2UI5: Show the Preview in an Editor Tab"** switch this setting and take a running app along, so the choice does not have to be made up front.

To reset the credentials, run the command **"abap2UI5: Clear Stored SAP Credentials"**.

enumDescriptions: Reload when the shown class is activated - with Ctrl+F3, or detected on the server when activated any other way (a save only marks the preview as "not activated").
Reload every time the shown class is saved - for setups in which saving already publishes the change.
Never reload on its own - use the reload button, the status bar or F9.
abap2ui5.reloadOn.markdownDescription:
When the preview of the shown app class reloads by itself.

- `activation`: on **Ctrl+F3** (*abap2UI5: Activate and Reload Preview*), which activates the class through your ABAP tooling and then reloads. An activation done any other way - the ABAP extension's own button, or Eclipse - is picked up too: while the preview is marked *not activated*, the class is watched on the server (through its ADT services) and the preview reloads as soon as it is active again. The **abap2UI5** output channel shows what the watch sees. Saving alone leaves the server on the active version, so it only marks the preview as *not activated*.
- `save`: on every save of the shown class.
- `never`: only on F9, the reload button or the status bar.

abap2ui5.reloadOnSave.markdownDescription: Reload the preview when the shown app class is saved.
abap2ui5.reloadOnSave.markdownDeprecationMessage: Replaced by `#abap2ui5.reloadOn#`. Saving does not change anything on the server - activation does. Still honoured while `abap2ui5.reloadOn` is unset: `false` behaves like `never`, `true` like `save`.

abap2ui5.viewCheck.onSave.markdownDescription:
Run the static view check every time a checkable file is saved: an ABAP class building views with `z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder`, or a raw `*.view.xml` / `*.fragment.xml`. Findings appear in the Problems panel. The command *"abap2UI5: Check Views (Static)"* runs the same check on demand.

To also apply every mechanical fix on save, opt in via VS Code's own setting:

```json
"editor.codeActionsOnSave": { "source.fixAll.abap2ui5": "explicit" }
```

abap2ui5.viewCheck.live.markdownDescription: Also check while typing, shortly after each pause. Only the bundled property gate runs on a keystroke - it works in-process and needs no I/O; the render gate stays on save and on demand.

abap2ui5.viewCheck.command.markdownDescription:
Command that runs the [abap2UI5-linter](https://github.com/abap2UI5/linter) CLI **for the render gate** - the property gate is bundled with the extension and needs no command. Leave empty for the default: a local checkout under `#abap2ui5.mcp.reposRoot#` when present (runs with VS Code's own Node.js), otherwise `npx --yes github:abap2UI5/linter` at the release commit of the linter this extension bundles.

Example for a local clone: `node /home/me/linter/cli.mjs`

This setting names a program the extension starts, so it is read from your user settings only - a cloned repository cannot point it somewhere else.

enumDescriptions: Not decided - the linter's own default. A control from a SAPUI5-only library is then reported as a hint: worth knowing, and the cue to write the distribution into the repository's abap2ui5lint.jsonc.
SAPUI5 - the distribution served by an ABAP system. Includes sap.ui.comp (Smart controls), sap.suite.*, sap.ushell, sap.fe and more; such controls are not reported.
OpenUI5 - the open-source distribution. Controls from SAPUI5-only libraries are reported as errors: they do not exist there.
abap2ui5.viewCheck.distribution.markdownDescription:
Which UI5 distribution the target system serves. SAPUI5 ships libraries OpenUI5 does not (`sap.ui.comp`, `sap.suite.*`, `sap.ushell`, `sap.fe`, `sap.viz`, ...), so a SmartTable is fine on SAPUI5 and a guaranteed runtime error on OpenUI5. With `openui5` such controls are reported as errors, with `sapui5` not at all; left unset, they are hints - the same answer a configless `abap2ui5lint` run gives.

A workspace's `abap2ui5lint.jsonc` wins over this setting - that is the file CI checks against.

abap2ui5.viewCheck.minUi5.patternErrorMessage: Must be a UI5 version like 1.71 or 1.120.3. A value that is not a version is silently ignored by the check, which then runs against the default floor.
abap2ui5.viewCheck.minUi5.markdownDescription:
The UI5 version to check against - **the version your system runs**. A control or property introduced after it is reported (it would not exist on your system), and a deprecation is only reported once it is in effect at that version. The metadata itself comes from the bundled snapshot; see the abap2UI5 output channel for the version it was generated from.

A workspace's `abap2ui5lint.jsonc` wins over this setting - that is the file CI checks against.

abap2ui5.viewCheck.render.markdownDescription:
Also run the render gate: the reconstructed view is loaded with a real `XMLView.create` in headless Chromium. Unlike the bundled property gate this needs the external checker - install it once with *"abap2UI5: Install Render Gate"* (downloads the checker bundle and Chromium, runs with VS Code's own runtime), or provide your own via `#abap2ui5.viewCheck.command#` / `#abap2ui5.mcp.reposRoot#`.

The render gate starts an external process over the repository's code, so this setting is read from your user settings only in Restricted Mode, and the gate does not run there at all until the workspace is trusted.

abap2ui5.viewCheck.rollingBundle.markdownDescription:
Download the render gate from the linter's **rolling** bundle instead of the immutable one published for the release commit of the linter version this extension build bundles.

Off by default, and worth leaving off: the rolling bundle is rebuilt on every merge to the linter's main branch, so the checker running on your machine can then change without this extension being updated. Turn it on only to try an unreleased linter.

It decides which program *"Install Render Gate"* downloads and runs, so it is read from your user settings only - a repository's `.vscode/settings.json` cannot switch it on.

abap2ui5.viewCheck.allow.markdownDescription:
Accepted deviations for the property gate, e.g. `sap.m.GenericTile.systemInfo` - each entry is passed to the checker as `--allow`. Merges with the `allow` list of a workspace's `abap2ui5lint.jsonc`.

To waive a single line rather than a whole rule, put the linter's own directive above it: `" abap2ui5lint-disable-next-line unknown-binding-path -- filled in a LOOP`. The quick fix on any finding writes it for you, and CI honours it too.

anyOf.description: report it at this severity instead of its default

exclude.description: file path patterns this rule does not judge

abap2ui5.viewCheck.rules.markdownDescription:
Which view-check rules are active, and how loudly. A rule id maps to `false` to switch it off, to `"hint"` / `"warning"` / `"error"` to change its severity, or to `{ "severity": …, "exclude": […] }`.

```json
"abap2ui5.viewCheck.rules": {
  "unknown-binding-path": false,
  "control-too-new": "warning"
}
```

A repository's `abap2ui5lint.jsonc` wins for every rule it names, so the editor keeps agreeing with CI about those; this setting decides the rest. Rule ids are listed on the [rules page](https://abap2ui5.github.io/linter/).

enumDescriptions: Errors and warnings only - the defects that are going to cost you something.
Nothing inline; the Problems panel and the squiggles are unaffected.
abap2ui5.inlineFindings.markdownDescription:
Show the view check's message at the end of the line it concerns, next to the squiggle. A builder chain is long and the Problems panel is far away, so the message is put where you are already looking.

Hints are off by default: they are worth knowing and never wrong by themselves, which in a forty-line chain is a lot of grey text for something you did not ask about.

abap2ui5.inlineSince.markdownDescription: Show the UI5 version a control or attribute arrived in, at the end of its line - warned when it is above `#abap2ui5.viewCheck.minUi5#`. The metadata ships with the extension, so this answers *"does my system have this yet?"* while you write the line rather than after the check runs.

abap2ui5.inlineDeprecated.markdownDescription: Show a control's or attribute's deprecation at the end of its line, with the replacement the UI5 documentation names. Deprecations and `#abap2ui5.inlineSince#` share one decoration pass; this switch governs only the deprecation half.

abap2ui5.inlineRoundtripCost.markdownDescription: Show what each **PUBLIC** attribute adds to a roundtrip, next to its declaration. abap2UI5 serializes every public attribute into the model on every roundtrip; the size is measured from the class's own literal seeds, or from a `<class>.mock.json` when there is one.

abap2ui5.renamePreview.markdownDescription:
Show the refactor preview when **F2** renames an event, a control id or a bound attribute, so every occurrence can be seen before it changes.

Those renames cross from ABAP into view literals on the strength of *where* a string stands - the one refactoring in this extension worth looking at first. Switch it off to rename straight away; the preview stays reachable with `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` in the rename box.

value.description: The theme name as it goes into the URL (sap-ui-theme), e.g. my_company_theme.

label.description: What the picker shows for it; the value itself when omitted.

value.description: The language key as it goes into the URL (sap-language), e.g. CS.

label.description: What the picker shows for it; the value itself when omitted.

abap2ui5.viewPreview.theme.markdownDescription: The UI5 theme *"abap2UI5: Preview View (No System)"* renders in. Any theme name the runtime ships, e.g. `sap_horizon`, `sap_horizon_dark`, `sap_fiori_3`, `sap_belize`.

abap2ui5.viewPreview.viewport.patternErrorMessage: Must be <width>x<height> in CSS pixels, like 1280x900 - or a comma-separated list such as 390x844,1280x900 for a device matrix.
abap2ui5.viewPreview.viewport.markdownDescription: The viewport(s) the systemless preview renders at, `<width>x<height>` in CSS pixels - e.g. `390x844` to see the view the way a phone lays it out. **Several, comma-separated, become a device matrix**: `390x844,1280x900` renders both in one browser session and shows them side by side. The picture is taken full-page, so a view taller than the viewport is shown whole.

abap2ui5.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer the [abap2UI5 MCP server](https://github.com/abap2UI5/mcp-server) to MCP clients in this window (Copilot agent mode and others). The server gives AI agents the abap2UI5 dev loop without an SAP system: capability queries, static view validation, deploy, build, headless run with screenshot.

abap2ui5.mcp.system.markdownDescription: Also offer the **abap2UI5 System** MCP server: real-system tools hosted by the extension itself - list the configured systems, search classes on the system (ADT quick search), run an app through the auth proxy with a headless screenshot, and - only with `#abap2ui5.agent.enableAppTools#` - operate an app through its JSON protocol. Uses the same credentials the preview stores; the run tool needs the render gate's Chromium.

abap2ui5.chatTools.markdownDescription: Offer the editor's chat three read-only tools for what only this window knows: the view check's findings of a document as the Problems panel shows them (`#abap2ui5Findings`), the XML view reconstructed from an app class (`#abap2ui5View`) and the live JSON model of the app shown in the preview (`#abap2ui5Model`, desktop only). None of them contacts or changes a system - the tools that do stay with the MCP servers (`#abap2ui5.mcp.system#`).

abap2ui5.agent.enableAppTools.markdownDescription: Allow the **abap2UI5 System** MCP server's app tools (`app_list`, `app_start`, `app_describe`, `app_act`) to operate abap2UI5 apps on the **real** active system: an AI agent fills fields and fires events through the abap2UI5 JSON protocol, **as the configured user** - an event runs for real and may save, post or delete data. Off by default; while it is off the tools stay listed and answer with how to allow them, sending nothing. User settings only: a workspace cannot turn it on.

abap2ui5.agent.confirmActions.markdownDescription: Ask before every acting step of the **abap2UI5 System** MCP server's app tools (see `#abap2ui5.agent.enableAppTools#`): each event an AI agent fires with `app_act`, and the first `app_start` of a class, opens a dialog naming the system, the class, the event, its arguments and the values sent with it - **Allow**, **Allow for This Session** (that class on that system, until the window closes) or **Deny**. Deny, or no answer within two minutes, tells the agent that you declined, and nothing is sent. On by default. User settings only: a workspace cannot turn it off.

abap2ui5.mcp.command.markdownDescription:
Command that starts the MCP server. Leave empty for the default: a local checkout under `#abap2ui5.mcp.reposRoot#` when present, otherwise `npx --yes -p @abap2ui5/mcp-server abap2ui5-mcp`.

Example for a local clone: `node /home/me/mcp-server/server.mjs`

This setting names a program the extension starts, so it is read from your user settings only - a cloned repository cannot point it somewhere else.

abap2ui5.mcp.reposRoot.markdownDescription:
Folder containing the checkouts the MCP server orchestrates (`abap2UI5`, `samples-controls`, `samples`, `samples-stack`, and optionally `linter`, `mcp-server`, `abap-cloud-gui`). The matching `A2UI5_HOME` / `SAMPLES_CONTROLS_HOME` / `SAMPLES_HOME` / `SAMPLES_STACK_HOME` / `AI_VIEW_CHECK_HOME` / `ABAP_CLOUD_GUI_HOME` environment variables are passed to the server, and local `mcp-server` / `linter` checkouts found here are preferred over downloading via npx.

What is found here decides which programs are started, so it is read from your user settings only.

abap2ui5.report2cloud.path.markdownDescription:
Folder of an [abap-cloud-gui](https://github.com/abap2UI5-addons/abap-cloud-gui) checkout (with `npm ci` done) whose converter *"abap2UI5: Migrate Classic Report to abap2UI5"* runs - report2UI5 in `tools/report2ui5`, or report2cloud in `tools/report2cloud` in a checkout of the addon's 1.0.0; it is not on npm. Leave empty to use the checkout `ABAP_CLOUD_GUI_HOME` names, the variable the MCP server's `migrate_report` reads for the same purpose, or else the copy *"abap2UI5: Install Report Converter"* downloaded.

It decides which program is started, so it is read from your user settings only.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with abap2UI5
walkthroughs.description: Launch an app with F9, keep the preview fresh on activation, and let the view check catch problems while you type.

steps.title: Point the extension at your system
steps.description:
Set the launch URL of your abap2UI5 endpoint - `{class}` is the placeholder for the app class.
[Set Launch URL](command:abap2ui5.setLaunchUrl)

steps.title: Run an app with F9
steps.description: With the cursor in a class implementing `z2ui5_if_app`, press F9 - the app opens next to the source.

steps.title: Activate and reload with Ctrl+F3
steps.description: Only activation changes what the server runs - Ctrl+F3 activates through your ABAP tooling and reloads the preview.

steps.title: Let the view check catch problems
steps.description:
Typos, too-new controls and dead bindings land in the Problems panel while you type.
[Check Views (Static)](command:abap2ui5.checkViews)

steps.title: Read the view as XML
steps.description:
See the XML the builder calls produce, live beside the class - findings mirrored, every line clickable.
[Show Reconstructed XML](command:abap2ui5.showReconstructedXml)

steps.title: Give your AI agent the dev loop
steps.description:
The bundled MCP server lets Copilot agent mode and friends build and run abap2UI5 apps without an SAP system.
[Show MCP Status](command:abap2ui5.showMcpStatus)

steps.title: Make your repository agent-ready
steps.description:
Add AGENTS.md, the four abap2UI5 skills, the MCP server and the two gates to the open project - nothing is overwritten, your classes are not touched.
[Add Agent Setup to Workspace](command:abap2ui5.addAgentSetup)
